verdict.rationale: Veriff documents the whole hosted path. You create a session server-side, send the user through its built-in front-end via a session URL, web/native SDKs or the in-page InContext embed, then read the result from a decision webhook or by polling the decision endpoint. Biometric liveness capture is available in the web flow and native SDKs, and the SDKs handle identity-document capture (NFC callbacks are mentioned). missing for 10: explicit documentation that one hosted flow combines document and selfie capture, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can launch a complete document-plus-selfie verification with a hosted or drop-in flow — create a session server-side, redirect or embed, and read the result — without building capture UI myself

citations.quote: Use this endpoint to **initiate a new verification session** for an end-user. Every verification flow begins with creating a session.
you prefer leveraging **Veriff's front-end solution**, wish to maximize the benefits of our **built-in verification flow**, and have **no plans to independently collect end-user media**
Veriff InContext solution allows your **end-users to go through the verification process within your web page**, maintaining uninterrupted workflow and reducing friction.
The purpose of the JS SDK is to create the session URL for your end-user's verification session.
Veriff sends decision webhooks immediately after making a decision
It is available via API, web flow, and native SDKs.
